quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When may drivers stop in travel lanes?

options.text: When they're lost.
When they are dropping off a passenger.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never stop in travel lanes. Not for any reason—being lost, a breakdown, or dropping off a passenger. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: On a slippery road, how should you adjust your following distance?

options.text: Keep it the same as normal.
Increase it—stay farther back than normal.
Decrease it—stay closer than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase it—stay farther back than normal.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, your car needs more distance to stop. Always increase your following distance when driving on wet, icy, or slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What should you do when passing on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away any oncoming cars are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away any oncoming cars are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming cars are moving. They may be closer or faster than they appear. Before passing, always make sure you can safely change lanes and that there is enough space. If you are unsure, wait until the oncoming car passes and you have a clear view of the road ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car ahead of you.
Drive carefully through and do not slow down to look at the area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through and do not slow down to look at the area.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to watch construction activity. This creates traffic jams. Drive carefully through the zone and keep your eyes on the road.

questions.question: If you park your car in an unusual spot, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
Park five feet away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked car does not become a hazard. No matter where you park, other drivers must be able to see your car from every direction.

questions.question: What does a red-painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
You can pick up or drop off passengers here.
No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.
questions.explanation: A red-painted curb means you cannot stop, stand, or park there—not even for a short time.

questions.question: What is the term for the amount of alcohol in your blood?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: How can you help the car behind you stay at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Drive at a steady speed and signal your turns, lane changes, and stops in advance. This helps the driver behind you predict your movements and maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test your vehicle's shock absorbers.
They make noise and vibration to alert drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make noise and vibration to alert drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create vibrations and noise to warn drowsy or distracted drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: When may you drive on the shoulder of the road?

options.text: Only when an official tells you to.
When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.
When the car in front of you is turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when an official tells you to.
questions.explanation: You may only drive on the shoulder of a road if an official has told you to do so.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, hay fever, allergies, and muscle relaxants. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug, whether illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse an alcohol test when a police officer asks?

options.text: Your license will be suspended.
It is your right and nothing will happen.
It is recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: When you drive a car in South Dakota, you automatically agree to an alcohol or drug test. If you refuse to take the test, your driving privileges will be suspended.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should drive slower and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights any time you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: The light is green, but traffic blocks the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles into the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if other vehicles are blocking your way, even if your light is green. If the light turns red while you are stuck in the intersection, you will block cross traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: What does this red and white sign tell you to do?

options.text: Stop and look both ways before going.
Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
Keep steady speed and watch for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop to let any vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian pass. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane is traveling faster than other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles on the road. Speeding increases your chance of a crash. Driving too slowly can cause rear-end collisions or force other drivers to swerve around you.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because of reduced visibility. You can only see as far as your headlights allow, which makes it difficult to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are traveling.

questions.question: Keep extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces. Bridge pavement can ice over even when the rest of the road is dry. Bridges also thaw out later than surrounding roads.

questions.question: How should you use the gas pedal?

options.text: Slowly and smoothly
As quickly as possible
By tapping it lightly

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and smoothly
questions.explanation: Press the gas pedal slowly and smoothly. Pressing it too quickly can make your wheels spin and cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: No one may pass.
Both sides may pass.
Only the right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops gradually and smoothly.

questions.question: If there is a single broken white line next to you on a highway, what can you do?

options.text: You cannot cross it to pass.
You may cross it to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross it to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross it to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.
